chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Musa ibn al-Hasan from Muhammad ibn al-Hamid from Abu Jamilyah al-Mufaddal ibn Salih from Zayd al-Shahham from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about a man who runs between al-Safa and al-Marwah without wudu (ablution), and he said, 'There is no objection.'

key_terms.الصَّفَا: Al-Safa, one of the two hills between which pilgrims run
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no objection / It is permissible
key_terms.وَالْمَرْوَةِ: And al-Marwah, the second hill in the Sa'i ritual
key_terms.وُضُوءٍ: Minor ablution (ritual washing of specific body parts)

ai.seo_question: Is wudu required for Sa'i between Safa and Marwah?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq clarifies that ritual purity (wudu) is not a prerequisite for Sa'i, distinguishing it from prayers where wudu is obligatory. This ruling highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding the physical state required for specific Hajj rituals, emphasizing that while cleanliness is recommended, it does not invalidate the act if absent. The hadith serves as a practical guideline for pilgrims who may find it difficult to maintain continuous wudu during the physical exertion of the seven circuits.
